points.ancienPropos: Q1 2026: the CFO explicitly says he is 'comfortable with double-digit EPS growth through the LRP' despite the WATCHMAN/EP headwinds already identified; WAMGR revised to '8% moving towards 9%' over the long-range plan horizon.
points.nouveauPropos: Q2 2026: WAMGR revised down again to '7-8%' (a loss of roughly 1 point vs Q1); 2027 now explicitly described as a 'transition year' with LIMITED adjusted EPS growth, the return to sustained EPS growth pushed out to 2028.
points.justification: In just three months, the message moves from explicit confidence in double-digit EPS growth across the whole long-range plan horizon to the announcement of a transition year with limited growth - a rapid and significant deterioration in the central trajectory of the thesis, beyond the usual routine quarterly guidance adjustment.

clesRetenues: Q Robbie Marcus (JP Morgan) - is the lowered guidance conservative so as to avoid further revisions, or does it reflect observed trends? How should 2027 organic growth (~5%) be thought about? - management indicates that 75% of the business is growing steadily at ~6%, EP and WATCHMAN being the drivers of the guidance cut; aim to improve 2027 relative to the H2 26 guidance, with an EP recovery expected in H2 27 and a significant improvement in 2028 thanks to the new launches (combined TAM >25 Md$).

Q Larry Biegelsen (Wells Fargo) - does 'no improvement in 2027' apply to the full year or only to H1? Impact of price cuts and of competition? Prospects for a first-line label after the CHAMPION-AF data? - management assumes the WATCHMAN market stays under pressure in 2027 until trends demonstrably improve, expects a competitor to enter in 2027 but maintains its confidence in WATCHMAN's market leadership.

Q Joanne Wuensch (Citi) - is the 2026 guidance (5-6% organic growth) a reasonable starting point for 2027? Which products carry the 2028 reacceleration? - management details seven major launches for 2028 and beyond (Penumbra closing, renal denervation system, TAVR option via MiRus, coronary IVL launch, entry into ICE, FARAWAVE Ultra, circulatory support); the ICVT segment positioned as the group's largest future growth driver.

Q Rick Wise (Stifel) - details on the 500M$ restructuring programme (timetable, reinvestment, P&L phasing)? - more than 50% of the savings realised by end-2027, first visible in SG&A in 2027 then in COGS later; the programme should allow operating margin expansion and strong EPS growth from 2028.

Q Mike Polark (Wolfe Research) - what can shift WATCHMAN prescribing patterns? New clinical data? Form-factor innovation? A path to a first-line label? - targeted investment in clinical education, broader commercial coverage and direct-to-patient marketing; SIMPLAAFY trial expected in H2 26; clinical trial of the WATCHMAN Elite device under way; seeking an FDA label update and a re-review of the CMS national coverage determination; 30-40% of AF patients requiring stroke prevention receive no treatment - substantial unmet need.

Q Travis Steed (BofA) - what EPS growth in 2027? Flat, in line with revenue, or with leverage? Path to double-digit growth in 2028? - limited 2027 EPS growth expected on account of gross margin pressure (WATCHMAN/EP weakness) and Penumbra dilution; restructuring and growth catalysts position a return to significant margin expansion and strong EPS growth from 2028.

Q Matt Taylor (Jefferies) - more precise expectations for EP growth in 2027? When do the pipeline products contribute? - H1 27 similar to the H2 26 dynamics; improvement in H2 27 with the FARAWAVE Ultra launch and entry into the ICE market; 2028 shows growth at or above market with Ultra, ICE and the FARAFLEX platform.

Q Jayson Bedford (Raymond James) - updated WAMGR? Market dynamics vs market share in sacral neuromodulation? - WAMGR now 7-8% (down roughly 1 point); urology expected flat to +1% for the full year 2026, improvement anticipated in 2027 with three cornerstone portfolio launches.

Q Robbie Marcus (JP Morgan) - timing of the guidance revision and validity of the long-range plan (LRP)? - three main drivers of the downward revision: WATCHMAN volume deceleration since mid-February, greater-than-expected EP market share erosion, and urology underperformance; management nonetheless says it is 'comfortable with double-digit EPS growth through the LRP' despite the 2026 headwinds.

Q Joanne Wuensch (Citi) - quarterly phasing through year-end? - Q2 identified as 'the toughest quarter' (demanding comps); WATCHMAN expected to grow low double digit for the rest of the year, EP mid-to-high single digit, the overall business mid single digit with acceleration in H2.

Q Larry Biegelsen (Wells Fargo) - EP market share pressure and US outlook? - US EP guided to mid single digit growth; three competitors identified (Medtronic, J&J, Abbott); despite the share erosion, management maintains 'high confidence' in retaining PFA leadership thanks to the pipeline launches.

Q Rick Wise (Stifel) - WATCHMAN outlook after the CHAMPION data and growth drivers? - the CHAMPION trial met all its primary and secondary endpoints; commercial and marketing investment to drive adoption; concomitant procedures expected to rise from 25% to 50% of the mix over the LRP horizon.

Q David Roman (Goldman Sachs) - growth excluding EP/WATCHMAN and product launches? - ICVT business executing at a very high level, AGENT and imaging exceeding expectations; FRACTURE trial data presented at EuroPCR (19 May 2026); interventional oncology growing high single digit in the tens of percent.

Q Travis Steed (BofA) - WAMGR trend and implications for the LRP? - revised WAMGR clarified at '8% moving towards 9%' over the LRP horizon; LRP organic revenue guidance judged premature at this stage, update planned after strategic planning.

Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore) - rationale for the 2 Md$ buyback given the Penumbra transaction? - the timing of the buybacks reflects cash availability and management's confidence in the company and its pipeline; buybacks starting after the lifting of the restriction tied to the Penumbra shareholder vote (6 May).

Q Matthew O'Brien (Piper Sandler) - commitment to the Penumbra transaction at the revised valuation? - closing expected in H2 2026 after the shareholder vote; management stresses the retention of Penumbra's sales force and R&D pipeline after closing.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Boston Scientific is a two-sided situation. Operational execution keeps beating: Q2 organic revenue +7% above guidance, adjusted EPS $0.86 (+15%) above the top of the range, FY25 closed at $3.06 (+22%). But the FY26 guidance has now been cut three times (initial $3.43-3.49 -> $3.28-3.32), driven by two genuine demand-side shocks: an unexpected US WATCHMAN slowdown (referral patterns hit by cumulative clinical evidence; standalone procedures down mid-teens) and competitive share loss in pulsed-field ablation (~80% of the US AFib market). Management frames 2027 as "more pressured than initially anticipated" with limited EPS growth, and a significant recovery in 2028 (FARAWAVE Ultra, intracardiac echo entry, Penumbra). The thesis rests on that 2028 re-acceleration plus the $500M run-rate restructuring savings by 2029 - while the historical guidance-sandbagging pattern (+7.9%/+11.6% beats vs initial anchors) is demonstrably broken this year, which is why the scorecard refinement is suspended.

== THESIS READ ==
- Third downward FY26 revision this quarter (EPS $3.28-3.32, organic 5-6%): WATCHMAN US slowdown and PFA share loss are demand facts, not execution noise.
- Q2 itself beat (organic +7%, adj EPS $0.86 above range top): the franchise executes; the issue is market trajectory, not delivery.
- 2027 explicitly guided as pressured with limited EPS growth; recovery narrative concentrated on 2028 (FARAWAVE Ultra, ICE market entry, Penumbra integration).
- Restructuring program: $500M run-rate savings by end-2029, more than half by 2027 - first visible in SG&A, then COGS.
- Watch: SIMPLAAFY results (late 2026) and potential FDA label updates for WATCHMAN - upside NOT embedded in current guidance.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
None.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: adjusted methodology (d-ter) - data carries the officially published adjusted results; data 2025 was retreated of $874M of true operating one-offs at the 03/08 refresh (E5 d-bis, published gross figures traced in that refresh). Normative tax 14% (AN confirmed); bridge established (c-ter): 2025 reconciliation leaves a +$327M residual to split from the 10-K (effective tax possibly below 14% that year); projections fit at 14% with rising net interest through the Penumbra debt peak (~$11.0B new debt, official), then an unallocated ~-$619M conservatism in 2030 flagged in AN-BRIDGE-PRUDENCE - deliberate safety margin, to arbitrate later. Penumbra (~$14.5B, cash + debt + shares) remains excluded from operating projections until closing; its financing is in omniumND from 2026-27. Scorecard: annualBeatPct +9.4% established but application SUSPENDED (regime break - see applicationNote). WATCH-LIST: (1) WATCHMAN US stabilization vs further referral erosion; (2) PFA share trajectory vs FARAPULSE roadmap; (3) Penumbra closing terms and first post-integration guidance; (4) 10-K split of the 2025 bridge residual; (5) restructuring savings pace vs charges. Next useful refresh: Q3 2026 results (late October).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 2026 results (late Oct); SIMPLAAFY readout (late 2026); Penumbra closing.

guidanceHistory.guidanceAnnuelle: Adj EPS cut to 3,28-3,32$ (vs 3,34-3,41$ at Q1 26); reported revenue cut to 5,5-6,5% (vs 7-8,5% at Q1 26). 3rd consecutive guidance cut since the start of the year.

epsReported.note: GAAP diluted EPS from the Q2 26 release (net income $907M; GAAP operating margin 21.6% incl. ~$75M product-liability charges partly offset by ~$80M IEEPA tariff refunds); adjusted $0.86.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: Revenue +3-5% (reported and organic) vs Q3 2025; adj EPS 0,80-0,82$ (guidance below the pre-release consensus).
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY2026 reported revenue +5,5-6,5% (organic +5-6%), adj EPS 3,28-3,32$ (excluding Penumbra) - 3rd guidance cut of the year.
pointsCles: Clean beat (organic revenue +7.0% at the top of guidance, adjusted EPS $0.86 +15% above the $0.82-0.84 range, mainly on favorable discrete tax items) - yet the THIRD FY26 guidance cut of the year: organic growth lowered to 5-6% and adjusted EPS to $3.28-3.32 (+7-8%), with Mahoney explicitly taking responsibility ('not the outcome we planned').

The cut is concentrated in the two 2024-25 hyper-growth engines (~25% of revenue): WATCHMAN - US LAAC market slowed sharply in ~6 months on compounding clinical evidence (OCEAN closure, CHAMPION confusion) hitting referrals for soft stand-alone indications (low-teens decline) while concomitant (now 1/3 of US procedures, +60% y/y) disrupted operations; and EP - US PFA penetration reached ~80-85% of the AF ablation market, limiting BSX's ability to offset underestimated competitive share loss (US +3% vs international +23%).

2027 explicitly framed as a transition year: revenue growth below the 7-8% WAMGR and LIMITED adjusted EPS growth (WATCHMAN/EP gross-margin pressure + slight initial Penumbra dilution), with H1 27 resembling H2 26; meaningful reacceleration expected in 2028 on 7 major launches exceeding a $25B cumulative TAM (coronary IVL SEISMIQ 4CE, TIVUS renal denervation, Penumbra, ICE entry, FARAWAVE Ultra, potential MiRus TAVR, circulatory support), plus WATCHMAN optionality on FDA labeling/CMS NCD.

New company-wide restructuring targeting ~$500M run-rate savings exiting 2029 (over half realized exiting 2027, SG&A first then COGS); $2B ASR completed (~40M shares, share count down to 1.475B), $1.5B MiRus investment with exclusive TAVR option, FY26 FCF ~$3.8B; the remaining ~75% of the business keeps growing ~6% with Neuromodulation +12%, Interventional Cardiology +15% and IO&E +12%.

ancrages.moteur: `data` 2025 had never been adjusted for the genuine operating exceptionals identified by management itself (874M$ pretax excluding amortisation: impairment 46M$, acquisition/divestiture 245M$, restructuring 343M$, litigation 194M$, EU MDR 46M$ - source: annual non-GAAP reconciliation from the 10-K FY2025), remaining at its raw GAAP level (EBIT 3450M$, margin 17,2%) - E5 d-bis compliance failure corrected at this refresh: EBIT adjusted to 4324M$ (margin 21,54%), net income adjusted to 3813M$ (same 'adjusted less amortisation retained' methodology applied consistently to the history and to the projections).

FY2026 adj EPS guidance cut to 3,28-3,32$ (vs 3,34-3,41$ at Q1 26, vs 3,43-3,49$ at the start of the year), reported revenue to 5,5-6,5% (vs 7-8,5%) - bottom-up build from actual H1 (normalised EPS 1,39$) + guided H2 (normalised EPS ~1,35$ after amortisation) giving a normalised FY2026 of 2,74$.

The CFO explicitly describes 2027 as a transition year with 'limited adjusted EPS growth' on account of the WATCHMAN/EP persistence and the initial Penumbra dilution, with a return to significant margin expansion and strong EPS growth pushed out to 2028 -> 2027 trajectory markedly flattened (+5% vs +16% in the previous thesis), reacceleration from 2028 carried by 7 product launches (combined TAM 25 Md$) and the restructuring savings.

The 10-K FY2025 now officially details the financing of Penumbra: ~11,0 Md$ of new debt (plus cash and a portion in shares), a ~14,5 Md$ deal in total, closing targeted for H2 2026 - a much heavier figure than the prudent assumption of the previous thesis -> omniumND revised markedly higher from 2026 (shifting towards ~18,5 Md$ at year-end), progressive deleveraging thereafter carried by FCF generation. The operating leg (revenue/EBIT) of Penumbra remains excluded from the projections for as long as the company has not published official post-closing guidance.

New restructuring programme announced this quarter, ~500M$ of recurring annual savings targeted exiting 2029 (more than half realised by end-2027, first in SG&A then in COGS) -> contributes to the modelled margin reacceleration from 2028-2029, on top of the product launches.
Normative tax rate maintained at 14% (consistent with the actual FY2025 effective rate of 14,57% - 493/3385 - once deferred/discrete tax items are neutralised), unchanged vs the previous thesis.

Intangible amortisation (897M$ pretax in 2025, ~466M$ in H1 2026 alone) retained in the normalised base as it is recurring at a serial acquirer such as Boston Scientific (and now Penumbra, under integration) - policy unchanged vs the previous thesis, reconfirmed by the Q2 2026 non-GAAP reconciliation.

Bridge (c-ter) exposes ~-$619M of unallocated conservatism in 2030 (and rising finNet 2028-29 while debt melts): the outer-year net trajectory embeds a deliberate safety margin on Penumbra integration and restructuring that is not decomposed line by line. To arbitrate at a future refresh: either name the components or release part of the margin.
